<x_0.1035><y_0.0>222 ENTOM C<x_0.9883><y_0.0195><class_Page-header>

<x_0.2402><y_0.0148>a great height; to accomplish which, they climb up some eminence, and are wafted about by the winds, filling the air with their threads. They are destroyed by the sphex and ichneumon.<x_0.9639><y_0.0813><class_Text>

<x_0.2432><y_0.0711>Linnaeus has subdivided this genus according to the number and position of their eyes.<x_0.9629><y_0.1102><class_Text>

<x_0.5098><y_0.1117>## A. Eyes eight.<x_0.7061><y_0.1305><class_Section-header>

<x_0.4434><y_0.132>1. _Eyes placed thus_, ::<x_0.7764><y_0.1531><class_Section-header>

<x_0.1025><y_0.157>_fasciata._ Of a silver colour ; the abdomen marked with yellowish bands ; the legs surrounded with brown rings. 48. A native of the island of Madeira.<x_0.9658><y_0.2016><class_Text>

<x_0.1123><y_0.1977>_diadema_ Abdomen nearly globular and reddish ; brown, mark- ed with a white cross composed of dots. 1. A native of Europe, on trees ; it is a very beautiful insect.<x_0.9688><y_0.2437><class_Text>

<x_0.1143><y_0.2406>_aquatica_ Brown ; abdomen oval and of an ash colour ; the back brown, marked with two dots. 39. A native of Europe, in stagnant waters, where it dives to the bot- tom in search of its food. It takes up its winter quar- ters in an empty snail shell, the aperture of which it closes up with a web ; jaws black, claws red.<x_0.9727><y_0.3297><class_Text>

<x_0.4482><y_0.3289>2. _Eyes placed thus_, :<x_0.7734><y_0.35><class_Section-header>

<x_0.1172><y_0.3563>_latro._<x_0.1924><y_0.3719><class_Section-header>

<x_0.2539><y_0.3492>Thorax hairy, and of an ash colour ; the abdominal oval, black, and spotted with red. 95. A native of America ; large, the thorax oval, legs black, thighs pale.<x_0.9775><y_0.4141><class_Text>

<x_0.1182><y_0.407>_domesti-_ Abdomen oval and brown, marked with five black spots nearly contiguous, the anterior ones larger than the others. 9. A native of Europe, in houses, and about windows ; feeds chiefly on flies.<x_0.9785><y_0.4711><class_Text>

<x_0.4248><y_0.475>3. _Eyes placed thus_,<x_0.7754><y_0.5><class_Section-header>

<x_0.1201><y_0.507>_globosa._<x_0.251><y_0.5281><class_Section-header>

<x_0.2588><y_0.5031>Black ; sides of the abdomen of a blood-red colour. 69. A native of Europe, in meadows.<x_0.9795><y_0.5422><class_Text>

<x_0.459><y_0.5453>4. _Eyes placed thus_,<x_0.7783><y_0.5672><class_Section-header>

<x_0.1211><y_0.5711>_argentata._<x_0.2568><y_0.5961><class_Section-header>

<x_0.2627><y_0.5719>Abdomen white, and brown behind, and marked round the edge with six small projections. 70. A native of South America.<x_0.9814><y_0.6227><class_Text>

<x_0.4658><y_0.625>5. _Eyes placed thus_,<x_0.793><y_0.6469><class_Section-header>

<x_0.1221><y_0.6562>_fumigata._<x_0.2559><y_0.6758><class_Section-header>

<x_0.2646><y_0.6523>Abdomen oval and brown, marked at the base with two white dots. 16. A native of Europe, in meadows ; it watches near the nests of the larvae of different insects, and waits their coming out, when it seizes on one after another, and sucks out their substance.<x_0.9863><y_0.7289><class_Text>

<x_0.1289><y_0.725>_saccata._<x_0.2598><y_0.7438><class_Section-header>

<x_0.2676><y_0.7234>Abdomen oval, of a brownish colour. 40. A native of Europe, in gardens, and carries its eggs behind it enclosed in a bag ; legs livid, marked with unequal brown rings set close together.<x_0.9902><y_0.7875><class_Text>

<x_0.4814><y_0.7883>_Eyes placed thus_, ::<x_0.7744><y_0.8063><class_Section-header>

<x_0.1357><y_0.8117>extensa.<x_0.2412><y_0.8273><class_Section-header>

<x_0.2686><y_0.8047>Abdomen long, of a silver colour tinged with green, the legs extended longitudinally. 22. A native of Europe, in woods ; its legs are applied closely to the branches.<x_0.9922><y_0.868><class_Text>

<x_0.1367><y_0.8664>_nidulans._<x_0.2578><y_0.8836><class_Section-header>

<x_0.2695><y_0.8625>Shining black ; the abdomen hairy and black. 73. A native of America ; it forms a nest under ground, and spins a large cylindrical web, which is covered with a lid ; its bite is very painful, and frequently oc- casions fever and delirium, which is soon removed by a<x_0.998><y_0.9414><class_Text>
